message.content:
Nxeon (Next.js/TypeScript/Prisma/Postgres, at /opt/nxeon) currently sells domains through exactly one registrar, name.com, via a reseller API. The owner now wants to ADD Namecheap and Enom as additional registrar backends, so that for every domain search, Nxeon queries all configured registrars, picks whichever is CHEAPEST after applying Nxeon's markup, and uses that registrar to actually fulfill the purchase — all while NEVER revealing which registrar was used to the customer (registrar identity must be admin-only). Design a concrete implementation plan for this. This is a planning/scoping exercise only — no code should be written.

## Current architecture (already audited)

**`lib/registrar.ts`** is the main name.com client — plain exported async functions (not a class), all hitting name.com's v4 REST API via a private `nc()` helper (`fetch` + HTTP Basic auth + `AbortSignal.timeout`). Key exports:
- `checkDomains(domains: string[]): Promise<DomainCheck[]>` — batched availability + pricing. `DomainCheck = {domain, available, premium, priceCents (retail), costCents (registrar cost), renewCents (retail renewal)}`.
- `registerDomain(domain, years, contact: RegistrantContact, purchaseCents)`, `renewDomain(domain, years, purchaseCents)`, `domainInfo(domain)`.
- Inbound transfer functions: `checkTransfer`, `createTransfer`, `getTransfer`, `cancelTransfer`, `listTransfers`, plus `transferOutcome`/`transferStatusLabel` (pure status-bucketing helpers, registrar-agnostic).
- DNS: `listRecords`, `addRecord`, `deleteRecord`, `getDnsHosts`.
- `registrarConfigured()`, `transfersAvailable()`.
- `domainMarkupPct()` reads an admin setting (`getSettingInt("domain_markup_percent", ...)`, clamped 0-500, default 25%) — ONE global markup applied uniformly. `retailCents(costCents, pct)` is the pure markup formula: `Math.round(costCents * (1 + pct/100))`.
- Just added: `disableRegistrarAutorenew(domain)` — calls name.com's own `:disableAutorenew` endpoint after every register/renew, because name.com has its OWN independent auto-renew flag (undocumented default, not settable at CreateDomain time) that could otherwise charge Nxeon's reseller account on its own schedule.
- SANDBOX mode (staging) has synthetic branches for `checkTransfer`/`createTransfer`/`getTransfer`/`cancelTransfer`/`listTransfers` (deterministic fake data, no real API calls) but NOT for `checkDomains`/`registerDomain`/`renewDomain`/`domainInfo` — those always hit whatever `NAMECOM_ENV` (`dev` = name.com's own separate sandbox API at api.dev.name.com, or `production`) points to.

**Two OTHER files independently duplicate a private name.com API client** (their own `nc()` helpers, NOT reusing lib/registrar.ts's):
- `lib/actions-domains-advanced.ts` — `updateNameservers`, `setWhoisPrivacy`, `requestTransferOut` (unlock + get auth code for outbound transfer).
- `lib/actions-domains-dns.ts` — some DNS-adjacent registrar calls (exact functions not yet enumerated, but confirmed to have its own `nc()` clone with the same `` `name.com: ${msg}` `` error-prefixing pattern).

This means there are currently 3 SEPARATE hardcoded name.com HTTP clients across the codebase, not one.

**`Domain` Prisma model** already has a `registrar: String` column (currently always hardcoded to the literal `"name.com"` at creation in `lib/actions-domains.ts`'s `registerDomainCore`, and again in the transfer-in path in `lib/actions-domains-transfer.ts`). This column is written but never read back to decide which API to call for an existing domain — every call site just imports functions from `lib/registrar.ts` etc. directly and assumes name.com unconditionally.

**Search/pricing entry point**: `lib/tools/domain-availability.ts`'s `checkAvailabilityBatched()` is the SHARED, cached (10min TTL, 4000-entry cap), batched (24 domains/call), globally-rate-limited (60 batches/min) wrapper around `checkDomains()` — used by BOTH the signed-out marketing `DomainChecker` and the signed-in dashboard `DomainSearch`/`DomainRegisterWizard`. This is the natural single choke point for multi-registrar fan-out on the SEARCH side. `app/api/domains/check/route.ts` calls this for the exact-domain + broad-TLD-catalog search shown in the wizard.

**Purchase-time re-check discipline (already established, must be preserved)**: `lib/actions-domains.ts`'s `purchaseDomain`/`registerDomainCore` NEVER trusts a price shown during search — it always calls `checkDomains([domain])` fresh immediately before charging (same anti-staleness principle as the "H2 incident" documented elsewhere in this codebase for VPS pricing). This same discipline naturally extends to multi-registrar: whichever registrar is cheapest gets decided FRESH at purchase time, not carried over from an earlier search snapshot.

## Confirmed customer-facing registrar-identity leaks (from a completed audit) that MUST be fixed as part of this work

1. `app/dashboard/domains/page.tsx:83` — nameserver label literally "Default (name.com)".
2. `app/dashboard/domains/[id]/page.tsx:346` — a `<Badge>` saying "name.com DNS".
3. `components/customer/DomainAdvanced.tsx:80,87` — "name.com" badge + "moves DNS off name.com's servers" copy.
4. `components/customer/DomainRedirects.tsx:68,72,147,219` — "live via name.com" / "name.com URL forwarding" copy (x3).
5. `lib/actions-domains.ts:344` — a customer-facing error string literally says "(name.com API keys missing)".
6. **Biggest leak vector**: raw registrar error messages (thrown as `` `name.com: ${msg}` `` from every `nc()`-style helper) flow UNMODIFIED through `errMsg()`-style catch handlers in `lib/actions-domains.ts`, `lib/actions-domains-dns.ts`, `lib/actions-domains-advanced.ts`, `lib/actions-domains-transfer.ts` and get returned as `{error: ...}` from server actions straight into customer components (`DomainRedirects.tsx`, `DomainAdvanced.tsx`, the register wizard, etc.) — so ANY registrar-side failure (e.g. the real "name.com: Payment failed" seen in production) is shown verbatim to the customer today, registrar name included.
7. `lib/actions-domains-advanced.ts`'s `setWhoisPrivacy()` returns a customer-facing `note` that interpolates `` `WHOIS privacy at ${domain.registrar} is provisioned...` `` — direct leak of the DB column.
8. `lib/kb-tools.ts:642` — `describeService()` includes `` `Registrar: ${domain.registrar}` `` as context fed to the AI live-chat assistant (mounted for signed-in customers) — the registrar name is available for the LLM to potentially echo back in an answer.

## Admin-side requirement

`app/admin/domains/page.tsx`'s domain table currently has NO per-row "Registrar" column at all (only a platform-wide "Registrar: name.com" stat card, hardcoded from env-var presence, not per-domain). The `Domain.registrar` column already exists in the DB and is already populated per-row — it just isn't displayed per-row today. Adding this column is straightforward once the column actually varies.

## What I need from you

A concrete, phased implementation plan covering:

1. **Consolidation first**: how to merge the 3 duplicate name.com HTTP clients (`lib/registrar.ts`, the ones in `lib/actions-domains-advanced.ts` and `lib/actions-domains-dns.ts`) into ONE `NameComRegistrar` implementation, before any second registrar is added — doing this after would mean writing the abstraction interface against 3 different existing call shapes at once.

2. **The abstraction interface**: what shape a `RegistrarClient` interface should take to cover EVERYTHING currently done per-registrar (checkAvailability, register, renew, domainInfo, DNS CRUD, inbound transfer lifecycle, nameserver updates, WHOIS privacy, outbound transfer/unlock/authcode, disableAutorenew) — and how dispatch should work: for a domain that already exists in the DB, look up `domain.registrar` and route to the matching client; for a NEW search/purchase, fan out to ALL configured clients.

3. **The price-shopping mechanism**: how `checkAvailabilityBatched` (or its replacement) should query multiple registrars per candidate domain and pick the cheapest AFTER markup, while preserving its existing cache/batch/rate-limit protections (each registrar is a separately metered, separately rate-limited third-party API — batching still needs to happen per-registrar, not merged). Confirm whether markup should be applied per-registrar-cost uniformly (so cheapest-cost == cheapest-retail == best-margin, avoiding a three-way tradeoff) or flag if you see a reason it shouldn't be.

4. **Real Namecheap and Enom API research**: what these two registrars' reseller/API programs actually require (account approval process, typical minimum balance/deposit requirements, auth mechanism, whether they have a sandbox/test environment analogous to name.com's api.dev.name.com, and their actual REST API shapes for availability/register/renew/DNS/transfer) — flag clearly that real API credentials and account approval are OWNER action items outside what code alone can deliver, and that sandbox testing may be limited if either lacks a real test environment.

5. **Fixing the leak surface**: a concrete, systematic approach (not necessarily fixing every file by hand) to guarantee no customer-facing surface — including error messages, AI chat context, and UI copy — can ever expose a registrar's name, while still letting admin views show it accurately per domain. Consider whether error messages need a customer-safe wrapper layer.

6. **Migration for existing data**: the one real domain that ever completed the FAILED-registration flow was just deleted, so there's no live ACTIVE domain currently in production needing a registrar re-classification — confirm whether any migration step is actually needed for existing rows, or whether this is clean-slate.

7. **Rollout/testing strategy**: given the codebase's established discipline (staging verification before every production promote, kill-switch settings for major changes, never re-quoting a price after checkout), propose a safe staged rollout (e.g., a settings flag to enable/disable each registrar independently, so name.com-only behavior is preserved until Namecheap/Enom are proven).

Please produce a structured, phased plan (not implementation code) that I can hand off almost verbatim into a plan document. Flag any open product decisions that need the owner's input rather than assuming an answer (e.g., exact minimum-balance/funding requirements you can't verify, or UX questions about how "best price, hidden registrar" should read on the customer search results page).

# Nxeon Multi-Registrar Implementation Plan

## Scope confirmation from codebase audit

I read all files named in the brief plus their neighbors. Two things worth flagging before the plan itself:

- **`prisma/schema.prisma:314`** — `Domain.registrar` currently defaults to `@default("namecheap")` in the schema, even though every write site hardcodes the literal `"name.com"`. This default has never been exercised (every row is explicitly set at create time), but it's a landmine for anyone who forgets to pass `registrar` explicitly in a future `db.domain.create()`. Fix the default as part of this work (see Phase 2).
- **Price-freeze timing is not uniform today**, which matters a lot for where the registrar decision must be frozen:
  - `purchaseDomain`'s **direct-wallet path** calls `checkDomains([domain])` fresh (`lib/actions-domains.ts:420`) immediately before charging.
  - `purchaseDomain`'s **card path** freezes `{priceCents, costCents}` into `DomainOrderIntent` at *session-creation* time (`lib/actions-domains.ts:457`, `prisma/schema.prisma:1941`), and `placeDomainCardOrder` → `registerDomainCore` never re-quotes — it trusts the frozen `priced` object, however old.
  - `registerDomainCore` (`lib/actions-domains.ts:140`) itself never calls `checkDomains` — it's purely a consumer of whatever `priced` it's handed.

  This means "decide cheapest registrar fresh at purchase time" actually has **two** freeze points, not one, and the registrar decision must be frozen at exactly the same moment as the price it's paired with — i.e. `DomainOrderPrice` and `DomainOrderIntent` both need a `registrar` field alongside `priceCents`/`costCents`, not a separate "re-decide which registrar" step at fulfillment. Getting this wrong would let a card order placed against a Namecheap quote silently fulfill through Enom if Enom becomes cheaper before the webhook fires — a customer never sees registrar, but the wrong backend gets charged/queried, which is an operational bug even if invisible to the customer.

---

## Phase 0 — Product decisions needed from the owner (blocking, before writing any code)

These aren't code questions; flagging them now so they don't stall Phase 3+ later.

1. **Namecheap/Enom account approval timeline and minimum balance.** I cannot verify current numbers (registrar reseller terms change and are gated behind an application); this is an owner action item, not something I can confirm from here. Do not let engineering estimate a launch date until:
   - Namecheap reseller/API application is submitted and approved (historically Namecheap requires an approved API access request tied to an account with API access enabled, and has posted account-age/spend thresholds for API keys in the past — needs verifying against Namecheap's current API documentation, not assumed).
   - Enom's reseller program is a paid-tier program (historically requires a setup fee / reseller agreement, distinct from Namecheap's free-with-threshold API access) — again, needs current verification, and Enom (owned by Tucows, same parent as name.com) may have a materially different account-approval bar than Namecheap.
   - Whether either program requires a **prepaid balance held at the registrar** (name.com reseller accounts typically work this way — cost is drawn from a prefunded balance) and what the practical minimum float is to avoid an order failing at checkout with money already taken from the customer's Nxeon wallet.
2. **Sandbox/test-environment parity.** name.com has a genuinely separate sandbox API (`api.dev.name.com`) that supports the SAME real endpoints (`checkAvailability`, register, renew) without real money moving. **Confirm before committing to a rollout date**: does Namecheap's/Enom's sandbox (if any) support live register/renew calls, or only availability checks? Namecheap has historically offered a sandbox (`api.sandbox.namecheap.com`) with restrictions (whitelisted IPs, limited TLD support, no real completions on some flows); Enom's test-environment story is less documented publicly. If either lacks a real registration sandbox, staging verification for that registrar's *purchase* path may be impossible pre-production, and the staged rollout plan (Phase 6) needs to lean harder on a small-dollar production canary instead of pure staging proof.
3. **Customer-facing UX for "best price, hidden registrar."** Today the search results just show one price per domain (from the single registrar). Once 2-3 registrars are queried, does the UI need to say anything at all about multi-sourcing (e.g. "price shown reflects our best available rate" ), or should the results page look byte-for-byte identical to today, just with occasionally different numbers? Recommend the latter (say nothing) since the requirement is registrar identity must be invisible — but confirm, since some product teams want a subtle "we shop multiple providers" trust signal even while hiding *which* one.
4. **What happens when registrars disagree on availability** (e.g. Namecheap says available, name.com says taken, for the same domain — this happens in practice due to registry sync lag). Recommend: treat "available" if ANY configured registrar says available and has a price; if registrars conflict, prefer the cheapest AVAILABLE quote and ignore the "taken" answers from others, but log the disagreement for ops visibility. Needs owner sign-off since it's a customer-trust question ("domain said available, purchase failed") more than a technical one — the existing `verifyRegistration`/needs-review machinery in `registerDomainCore` already handles the failure path if the winning registrar's availability turns out stale by purchase time, so this is a rare-case UX/messaging call, not a gap.
5. **Markup model — confirmed no open question, recommend uniform global markup stays.** Applying `domainMarkupPct()` uniformly to whichever registrar's `costCents` wins avoids a three-way tradeoff (cheapest-cost, cheapest-retail, and best-margin-for-Nxeon all become the same registrar automatically, since `retailCents = cost * (1 + pct)` is monotonic in `cost` for a fixed `pct`). The only way this breaks is if a future requirement wants *per-registrar* markup percentages (e.g. Namecheap costs more but Nxeon wants a thinner margin there for competitive reasons) — flag that as an explicit non-goal for this phase unless the owner says otherwise, since per-registrar markup would reintroduce exactly the tradeoff uniform markup avoids.

---

## Phase 1 — Consolidate the 3 name.com clients into one `NameComRegistrar`

**Do this before writing the abstraction interface**, per the brief's own reasoning: designing `RegistrarClient` against 3 slightly-different existing call shapes at once is how the interface ends up wrong in three different ways.

1. ## Phase 2 — The `RegistrarClient` abstraction

### Interface shape

Rename `lib/registrar.ts`'s contents into a `NameComRegistrar` implementation of a new interface, e.g. `lib/registrars/types.ts`:

```
interface RegistrarClient {
  readonly id: string;              // "namecom" | "namecheap" | "enom" — DB value, admin-only
  readonly label: string;           // "name.com" | "Namecheap" | "eNom" — admin display only
  isConfigured(): boolean;

  // Search / pricing
  checkDomains(domains: string[]): Promise<DomainCheck[]>;   // same DomainCheck shape as today

  // Lifecycle
  registerDomain(domain, years, contact, purchaseCents): Promise<{expiresAt?: Date}>;
  renewDomain(domain, years, purchaseCents): Promise<void>;
  domainInfo(domain): Promise<{expires?: Date; created?: Date}>;
  disableRegistrarAutorenew(domain): Promise<void>;   // best-effort, per registrar's own auto-renew quirk

  // Inbound transfer
  checkTransfer(domain): Promise<TransferCheck>;
  createTransfer(domain, authCode, purchaseCents): Promise<TransferInfo>;
  getTransfer(domain, startedAt?): Promise<TransferInfo | null>;
  cancelTransfer(domain): Promise<TransferInfo>;
  listTransfers(): Promise<TransferInfo[]>;

  // DNS
  listRecords(domain): Promise<DnsRecord[]>;
  addRecord(domain, rec): Promise<void>;
  deleteRecord(domain, id): Promise<void>;
  getDnsHosts(domain): Promise<DnsHost[]>;

  // Nameservers / WHOIS / outbound transfer (from Phase 1's consolidation)
  setNameservers(domain, nameservers): Promise<void>;
  getAuthCode(domain): Promise<string>;
  unlockDomain(domain): Promise<void>;
  lockDomain(domain): Promise<void>;
  getDomainLockStatus(domain): Promise<boolean>;
  listForwardings(domain): Promise<Redirect[]>;
  setForwarding(domain, host, forwardsTo, type): Promise<void>;
  deleteForwarding(domain, host): Promise<void>;
}
```

`transferOutcome`/`transferStatusLabel` stay as free pure functions (registrar-agnostic status bucketing, confirmed in the audit) — they operate on a raw status string regardless of which registrar produced it, no reason to put them on the interface.

`domainMarkupPct()`/`retailCents()` also stay free functions, outside any one client — markup is a platform-level concept applied *after* any client returns a cost, not a per-registrar behavior (reinforces the Phase-0 #5 answer).

### Registry / factory

Add `lib/registrars/index.ts` exporting:
- `ALL_REGISTRARS: RegistrarClient[]` — one entry per implementation (`NameComRegistrar`, `NamecheapRegistrar`, `EnomRegistrar`), each gated by its own env-var presence check inside `isConfigured()`, mirroring today's `registrarConfigured()` pattern per-registrar instead of one global check.
- `configuredRegistrars(): RegistrarClient[]` — filters `ALL_REGISTRARS` by `isConfigured()` AND a new per-registrar admin settings kill-switch (Phase 6) so an owner can disable a registrar without touching env vars.
- `registrarById(id: string): RegistrarClient | undefined` — for dispatch by `domain.registrar`.
- `anyRegistrarConfigured(): boolean` — replaces today's single `registrarConfigured()` at call sites that just need "is domain stuff usable at all" (e.g. gating the dashboard nav item), not "which one."

### Dispatch rule (the core design decision)

- **Existing domain (has a DB row)**: every call site that currently does `import { X } from "./registrar"` and calls `X(domain.name, ...)` changes to `registrarById(domain.registrar)?.X(domain.name, ...)`, with a clear error if that registrar is no longer configured (e.g. owner disabled Namecheap after some customers already have Namecheap-fulfilled domains — those existing domains must keep working against Namecheap specifically, not silently fail over to name.com, since name.com has no record of that domain). This affects: `worker/billing.ts`'s `domainAutoRenewSweep` (renew), the transfer-status poller, every DNS/nameserver/WHOIS/redirect/lock action in the consolidated Phase-1 files, and `verifyRegistration`'s post-failure check in `registerDomainCore`.
- **New search/quote (no DB row yet)**: fan out to `configuredRegistrars()` — this is Phase 3.
- **New inbound transfer quote** (`checkTransfer` in `lib/actions-domains-transfer.ts`): same fan-out-then-cheapest logic as a new registration search, since an inbound transfer hasn't picked a destination registrar yet either. `createTransfer` then targets whichever registrar won the quote, and that registrar's `id` is what gets written to `Domain.registrar` for the transferred-in row (replacing the current hardcoded `"name.com"` at `lib/actions-domains-transfer.ts:245`).

## Phase 3 — Price-shopping mechanism in `checkAvailabilityBatched`

Constraints to preserve, per-registrar (each is separately metered/rate-limited):
- Its own cache TTL/cap — fine to keep ONE shared cache map, but the cache **key must become `(registrarId, domain)`**, not just `domain`, since name.com's $12.98 and Namecheap's $11.49 for the same domain are different facts that both need to live in cache independently (the *result* shown to the customer is derived — "cheapest of the cached per-registrar entries" — not itself the cached unit).
- Its own batch size (`BATCH_SIZE` today is name.com-specific at 24; Namecheap/Enom need their own verified-safe batch sizes — do not assume 24 works for both, this needs empirical verification against each registrar's actual `checkAvailability`-equivalent endpoint once sandbox/test credentials exist).
- Its own rate-limit bucket key — replace the single `"registrar:availability:global"` `checkRateLimit` key with `` `registrar:availability:${registrarId}:global` ``, each with its own `GLOBAL_BATCHES_PER_MIN` (per-registrar, since a shared budget would mean an Enom outage or slow response artificially throttles name.com lookups too).

Restructured flow for `checkAvailabilityBatched(domains)`:
1. For each configured registrar, run today's existing per-registrar algorithm unchanged (own cache read, own batching, own rate-limit gate, own `try/catch` degrading to `unknown`) — i.e. `Promise.allSettled` across `configuredRegistrars().map(r => checkAvailabilityForRegistrar(r, domains))`, each returning a `Map<domain, DomainCheck | "unknown">` for that registrar alone.
2. Merge: for each domain, look at every registrar's result; pick the entry with the lowest `priceCents` among those with `available === true && priceCents !== null`; if none are available, the domain is `"taken"` only if at least one registrar explicitly said taken — if every registrar came back `unknown` (all throttled/erroring), the merged result is `unknown`, never a fabricated "taken."
3. `AvailabilityOutcome` needs one added field for internal/admin use only, never exposed to the customer-facing `DomainResult` type: which registrar won, so `purchaseDomain`'s fresh re-check (Phase parallel below) and the eventual `Domain.registrar` write have something to persist. Recommend a SEPARATE return shape used only server-side (e.g. `checkAvailabilityBatched` keeps today's public `DomainResult[]` untouched for anything rendering to the browser, and a new `checkAvailabilityBatchedInternal` — or an optional `includeRegistrar` flag — is what `purchaseDomain`'s fresh pre-charge check and `app/api/domains/check/route.ts` behind-the-scenes plumbing call). This is the concrete mechanism that keeps registrar identity from ever reaching a client bundle or API response by construction, not just by convention.
4. `formatPrice` and everything customer-facing stays untouched — the merge happens before `toResult()`, so `toResult` never even receives a registrar id to accidentally leak.

**The purchase-time re-check** (`checkDomains([domain])` at `lib/actions-domains.ts:420`) needs the equivalent single-domain fan-out: replace that call with a helper (e.g. `quoteCheapest(domain): Promise<{registrar: string; check: DomainCheck} | null>`) that queries all configured registrars for the one domain fresh (no cache — this is the anti-staleness check, deliberately bypassing the 10-minute TTL cache used for search) and returns the winner. This is what makes `DomainOrderPrice` need a `registrar` field, and what `registerDomainCore` uses to pick which `RegistrarClient` to call for `registerDomain`/`disableRegistrarAutorenew`, and what gets written to `Domain.registrar` at `lib/actions-domains.ts:202` instead of the current hardcoded `"name.com"`.

I can outline what these programs are known to generally require, but I'm flagging plainly: **I have not verified current-as-of-2026 terms against either registrar's live documentation**, and specific numbers (deposit minimums, approval SLAs) change. Treat the below as "what to go verify," not "what to build against."

**Namecheap:**
- Reseller/API access has historically been gated behind an account meeting a minimum age/spend threshold (their public API docs have stated thresholds like a minimum number of domains under management or account balance before API keys are issued) rather than a separate paid reseller tier — needs re-verification at signup time.
- Auth: API key + username + whitelisted client IP (Namecheap's API is IP-allowlist gated, unlike name.com's plain HTTP Basic — this is an operational difference: Nxeon's production egress IP(s) must be registered with Namecheap and kept in sync if infra changes).
- Sandbox: Namecheap has historically offered `api.sandbox.namecheap.com` with its own separate account/API key, similar in spirit to name.com's `api.dev.name.com` — but confirm current TLD coverage and whether registration/renewal calls actually complete in sandbox or only availability checks work.
- API shape: XML-based responses (not JSON like name.com v4) via query-string GET requests per command (`namecheap.domains.check`, `namecheap.domains.create`, `namecheap.domains.renew`, `namecheap.domains.dns.setHosts`, `namecheap.domains.transfer.create`) — this is a materially different response-parsing shape than name.com's JSON REST, so `NamecheapRegistrar`'s implementation needs an XML parser (`fast-xml-parser`, already a dependency per `package.json`) rather than `res.json()`.

**Enom:**
- Enom (Tucows-owned, same parent company as name.com/OpenSRS) has historically run a more traditional paid reseller program with its own account setup — confirm current terms; do not assume it mirrors name.com's terms just because they share a parent.
- Auth: username + API password/token via query-string GET, response format historically XML by default with a JSON option on newer endpoints — confirm which is current.

The consolidation win from Phase 1 is entirely about eliminating name.com's OWN duplication, not about sharing HTTP plumbing across different registrars' incompatible APIs.

## Phase 5 — Eliminating the leak surface

The 8 confirmed leaks split into two categories that need different fixes:

**A. Static UI copy (leaks #1–4, hardcoded strings)** — mechanical find-and-replace, but do it via a single source of truth so it can't regress:
- Introduce one constant, e.g. `lib/registrar-copy.ts` exporting `REGISTRAR_NEUTRAL_LABEL = "our registrar partner"` (or whatever the owner prefers per Phase-0 UX input) and a helper like `dnsProviderLabel()` for the handful of places that need to say *something* generic ("Default (our registrar)", "DNS records", "moves DNS off our registrar's servers", "live via our registrar", "our registrar's URL forwarding"). Replace `app/dashboard/domains/page.tsx:83`, `app/dashboard/domains/[id]/page.tsx:346`, `components/customer/DomainAdvanced.tsx:80,87`, `components/customer/DomainRedirects.tsx:68,72,147,219` to use it instead of the literal string.
- Add a lint-able guard: a `test/` unit test (this codebase already has `npm test` via `tsx --test test/*.test.ts`) that greps `components/customer/**` and `app/dashboard/**` for the literal strings `"name.com"`, `"namecheap"`, `"enom"` (case-insensitive) and fails the build if found outside an explicit allowlist (e.g. admin-only files). This turns "don't leak the registrar" from a one-time fix into a standing invariant that survives future PRs — genuinely important here since 3 registrars means 3x the surface for a future contributor to accidentally hardcode one by name in a new customer-facing string.

**B. Dynamic leaks (#5–8, values that flow through at runtime)** — these need a structural fix, not string replacement, because the leaking value is user/registrar-controlled at runtime:

1. **Error messages (#6, the biggest vector).** Every `nc()`-style helper across the 3 (soon-to-be-1, post-Phase-1) clients throws `` `${registrarLabel}: ${msg}` ``. Introduce a **customer-safe error wrapper** at the `RegistrarClient` boundary, not at each of the ~15 call sites that currently do `` `...: ${errMsg(e)}` ``. Concretely: every `RegistrarClient` implementation's private HTTP helper throws a typed `RegistrarError` class carrying `{registrarId, rawMessage, customerMessage}`, where `customerMessage` is a generic, registrar-name-free string derived from the raw one (e.g. pattern-match known categories — "insufficient balance"/"payment failed" at the registrar → "We couldn't complete this with our registrar right now — no charge was made, please try again or contact support"; anything unrecognized → a generic fallback, never the raw string). Server actions that currently do `return { error: errMsg(e) }` or interpolate the message into a customer-facing string switch to reading `e.customerMessage` when `e instanceof RegistrarError`, and keep logging `e.rawMessage` (with registrar id) server-side for ops/audit. This is the single highest-leverage change in Phase 5 — it closes leak #6 (the actual "name.com: Payment failed" production incident referenced) at the source for all current AND future registrars, rather than patching call sites one at a time as they're discovered.
2. **`lib/actions-domains.ts:344`** ("(name.com API keys missing)") — becomes generic: "(domain registration is not configured yet)", since with 3 possible registrars there's no single "the keys" to name anyway; this reads more correctly once there are 3 independent configuration states.
3. **`setWhoisPrivacy`'s note (#7)** — drop the `${domain.registrar}` interpolation entirely; the note doesn't need to name the registrar to be informative ("Preference saved. WHOIS privacy is provisioned at registration — contact support to change it on a live domain.").
4. **`lib/kb-tools.ts:642` (#8)** — remove `Registrar: ${domain.registrar}` from `describeService()`'s context string entirely. The AI assistant has no legitimate need to know or potentially echo which registrar backs a domain; this is pure risk with no product value, so delete rather than reword. (Everything else on that line — `whoisPrivacy`, `autoRenew` — stays; only the registrar field is a leak risk.)

**Admin side (the one place registrar identity SHOULD show):** add a "Registrar" column to `app/admin/domains/page.tsx`'s table (currently 6 columns ending at "Expires" — insert one before or after "Status"), rendering `d.registrar` directly (e.g. via a `Badge`) — this is a pure additive change since the column already exists and is already populated per-row. Also update the page's top-of-page stat card (`"Registrar" / "name.com" or "Not connected"` at line 37-42) — with 3 possible registrars this single stat card no longer makes sense as one value; replace it with either 3 stat cards (one per registrar's configured/not-configured state) or a small per-registrar status list, and update the page's static header copy ("Customer domain registrations via name.com.") to drop the specific name.

## Phase 7 — Rollout / testing strategy

Following the codebase's established discipline (kill-switches, staging-first, never re-quote after checkout):

1. **Ship Phase 1 (consolidation) alone first**, to production, behind nothing (it's a pure refactor with no new registrar and no behavior change) — get it soaking with real traffic before any multi-registrar logic lands on top of it. This isolates "did the refactor break name.com" from "did adding Namecheap break something."
2. **Add per-registrar admin settings kill-switches** in `lib/settings.ts`'s `SETTINGS_DEFAULTS`, e.g. `registrar_namecom_enabled` (default `"true"`, preserving today's only-registrar behavior), `registrar_namecheap_enabled` (default `"false"`), `registrar_enom_enabled` (default `"false"`). `configuredRegistrars()` (Phase 2) checks both `isConfigured()` (env vars present) AND the matching setting, so a registrar with real credentials loaded can still be held back from live traffic until proven. This mirrors the existing `kb_bot_enabled` pattern in the same settings file.
3. **Ship the `RegistrarClient` abstraction + fan-out logic with Namecheap/Enom flags OFF** — behaviorally identical to today (only name.com configured+enabled), but now running through the new dispatch path. This isolates "did the abstraction introduce a regression in the name.com-only case" from "does Namecheap/Enom actually work," which is the same staged-verification principle the codebase already applies elsewhere (e.g. `NAMECOM_ENV=dev` sandbox before production promote).
4. **Enable Namecheap in staging first**, once sandbox credentials exist, and run through: availability search (verify batching/pricing shape), a full registration in whatever sandbox exists (or, if Namecheap's sandbox doesn't support real completions, a very small real-money production registration as the actual first proof — flagged in Phase 0/4 as a real possibility), renewal, DNS CRUD, nameserver update, WHOIS toggle, outbound transfer unlock/authcode, inbound transfer quote+submit+poll+cancel. Only then flip `registrar_namecheap_enabled` on in production, initially perhaps gated further to a small traffic percentage if the codebase has (or this work adds) any existing percentage-rollout mechanism — otherwise a straight on/off flag is consistent with how `kb_bot_enabled` and similar flags already work here.
5. **Repeat step 4 for Enom independently** — do not enable both simultaneously for the first production exposure; if something goes wrong with the merged cheapest-price logic (e.g. a malformed Enom response corrupts the fan-out merge and picks a bogus "cheapest" price), isolating to one newly-added registrar at a time makes the kill-switch (turn that one setting off) an immediate, precise mitigation rather than "turn off all multi-registrar behavior."
6. **Monitor via the existing audit-log/needs-review machinery** — `registerDomainCore`'s existing `verifyRegistration`/needs-review path already handles "registrar call failed, unclear if it went through" per registrar (since it's dispatched through `registrarById(domain.registrar)` post-Phase-2); no new monitoring primitive is needed, just confirm the existing admin views that surface `needs_review`/`FAILED` domains also show the `registrar` column (Phase 5's admin table addition) so ops can tell which backend is producing failures.
7. **Explicitly do NOT test the "hidden registrar" property with a UI check alone** — add the Phase-5B static-string test (`test/` grep guard) to CI so it runs on every PR going forward, not just once at launch. This is the actual regression-proofing for the "never reveal registrar identity" requirement, since a manual QA pass at launch won't catch a leak introduced 6 months later by an unrelated feature PR.
